title: Media Systems
summary: A sanitized view of resilient streaming interfaces—from newsroom and network-player shells to the portfolio's testable MSE/HLS package—where captions, recovery, and clear state matter as much as the bits on the wire.
role: Senior Innovation Software Engineer — UI architecture, playback UX, captions and control racks, prototyping, and package boundaries
timeframe: NBCUniversal / NDP player experience through ongoing @tgmc/media-player development
problem: Streaming interfaces have to stay understandable while network conditions, browser capabilities, manifests, ads, captions, and playback state change underneath them—often on the same pages that also carry live data graphics.
constraints: Employer details, proprietary ad paths, and unpublished outcomes remain sanitized.
Playback behavior varies across browsers, codecs, network conditions, and content-protection boundaries.
Control racks, caption cards, and failure states must help viewers recover without exposing implementation noise.
Browser-safe media utilities must stay separated from server and packaging boundaries so the same ideas travel into a public Nx package.
approach: Model playback as explicit states the interface can explain rather than a single opaque loading condition.
Treat captions, accessibility affordances, and ad/interrupt paths as first-class UX—not afterthoughts bolted onto a transport layer.
Separate browser-safe media utilities from server and packaging boundaries; exercise them with unit tests, demos, and repeatable build targets.
Use progressive enhancement so unsupported paths fail clearly and preserve a useful next action.
Keep media UX aligned with the broader experience-system grammar: visible state, recovery, and inspectable proof.

evidence.label: Platform proof
evidence.value: Sanitized NDP / newsroom player work: control racks, caption card UI, and HLS/media adapters under real network variance

evidence.label: Implementation proof
evidence.value: @tgmc/media-player MSE/HLS workspace package with browser-safe entry points

evidence.label: Quality proof
evidence.value: Unit-tested utilities and a supporting /media-player demonstration

evidence.label: Architecture proof
evidence.value: Nuxt/Nx package boundaries that mirror how product UX and transport concerns stay split
